title: auth-scope microbenchmarks
question: What does each step of auth evaluation cost, in isolation from storage?
conclusions: In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU), evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants (cap), match last is 42.26x slower than evaluateGrantStack: 2 grants
In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > group principals, 10 grants, group of 1000 members is 55.41x slower than 10 grants, group absent from the map
In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > conditions, evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants x 100 condition nodes is 2632.94x slower than evaluateCondition: single comparison
In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > auth scope write validation, retention: 100 grants, administered from the bottom is 5187.43x slower than retention: 10 grants, administered from the top
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead), L4_AUTH_CONDITIONS: 100 grants is 6.35x slower than L0_CLEAN: 100 grants
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead) > group fan-out at L3, 5 distinct group(s) is 2.8x slower than 1 distinct group(s)
In read gate (scopePredicate), ModelReadGate: 100 grants is 18.05x slower than ModelReadGate: uninitialized policy (fast path)
In read gate (scopePredicate) > group roster serving, 100 referencer(s), reader outside the audience is 57.83x slower than 1 referencer(s), reader outside the audience

title: write-cache microbenchmarks
question: What does a write-cache hit and miss cost against PGlite?
conclusions: In Write Cache Cold Miss Performance, Cold miss rebuild (1000 operations) is 78.29x slower than Cold miss with keyframe optimization (100 ops, keyframe at 50)
In Write Cache Hit Performance, Cache hit with multiple revisions in ring buffer is 1.14x slower than Cache hit (latest revision)
In Write Cache Warm Miss Performance, Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations) is 6.86x slower than Warm miss with nearby cached revision
In Write Cache LRU Eviction Performance, LRU eviction (filling cache to capacity) is 3.02x slower than LRU access pattern (updating access order)
In Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline, With cache: rebuild (1000 operations) is 62.33x slower than No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (100 operations)
In Write Cache Keyframe Performance, Keyframe persistence overhead (every 10th revision) is 1x slower than Without keyframe persistence (interval = 1000000)
caveats: The no-cache baseline compares a cold cache rebuild against a manual replay, and a cold rebuild is a replay, so that pair reads about 1x by construction rather than measuring what the cache is worth
The two keyframe cases are floored by a 100ms drain sleep that lets fire-and-forget keyframe writes land, so their difference is not a measure of persistence overhead
Write Cache Cold Miss Performance / Cold miss rebuild (1000 operations): 10 samples, too few for the spread to mean much
Write Cache Warm Miss Performance / Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations): 52 samples, too few for the spread to mean much
Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline / No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (1000 operations): 10 samples, too few for the spread to mean much
Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline / With cache: rebuild (1000 operations): 10 samples, too few for the spread to mean much
Write Cache Keyframe Performance / Keyframe persistence overhead (every 10th revision): 10 samples, too few for the spread to mean much
Write Cache Keyframe Performance / Without keyframe persistence (interval = 1000000): 10 samples, too few for the spread to mean much
